title: FAT-TAG: Mitigating Forgetting in Task-Free Temporal Graph Class Incremental Learning

problem.claim: Graph Class Incremental Learning must handle continuously arriving class sequences while accounting for temporal dependencies and task-free inference.

gap.claim: Existing studies often overlook explicit temporal dependencies in evolving graphs and rely on predefined task boundaries or task identifiers, limiting applicability to genuinely task-free scenarios.

contributions.claim: FAT-TAG uses temporal graph tokenization to preserve structural dependencies and represent temporal precedence for the Graph Transformer.
FAT-TAG uses Freeze-and-Adapt Training, training the Graph Transformer backbone only on the initial task and adding a lightweight Low-Rank adapter for each subsequent task.
FAT-TAG uses a Time-Aware Gate to route instance-level samples to LoRA adapters without task identifiers for task-free inference.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments across four real-world temporal graph benchmarks reportedly show that FAT-TAG consistently surpasses state-of-the-art baselines in mitigating forgetting.
The source code is reported to be available at the linked repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: Class Incremental Learning trains continuously on task sequences with distinct class sets, and its graph setting adds further challenges.
Prior graph methods are described as missing explicit temporal dependencies and depending on task boundaries or identifiers, restricting task-free use.
FAT-TAG addresses the setting through temporal graph tokenization, Freeze-and-Adapt Training with lightweight adapters, and a Time-Aware Gate for task-free routing.
The authors report benchmark results against state-of-the-art baselines and provide a source-code link.

source_observation.claim: Explicit temporal dependencies and task-free inference are identified as distinct challenges in graph class-incremental learning.

interpretation.claim: A continual-learning design may need to model temporal structure directly rather than represent time only through ordered task slices.

application.claim: For evolving graph systems, consider temporal representations and inference mechanisms that do not require externally supplied task identifiers.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether these mechanisms generalize beyond the reported temporal graph benchmarks.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the four benchmarks, dataset sizes, metrics, or experimental settings.
The abstract does not provide quantitative results or ablation findings.
The abstract does not describe the tokenization procedure, adapter configuration, or gate-training details.
